title: Capacity operational playbook + monthly heatmap (rolling buffer)
summary: Working operational plan to convert monthly regional forecasts into an actionable rolling buffer schedule across NA / EU / APAC. Focus is on fast reaction windows (weekly run rate checks), spot vs reserved mix, and thermal/instance-type constraints that affect effective capacity. This doc contains assumptions, 3 demand scenarios, an actionable trigger matrix, and a compact monthly heatmap (next 9 months) for planning and oncall playbooks.
objectives: 1) Provide a single-pane operational playbook that SREs and capacity planners can use to decide region-specific onboarding or throttles within a 72-hour window. 2) Define buffer trigger thresholds (soft/hard) and automated remediation candidates (scale up, route-to-tier, degrade-quality). 3) Surface instance-type and quantization impact on usable token throughput per GPU. 4) Produce a rolling 9-month heatmap aligned with sales signals and feature launches.
assumptions_and_inputs: - Baseline utilization: 65% fleet-wide (August 2025 telemetry). - Typical request distribution by region (tokens): NA 52%, EU 30%, APAC 18%. - Model mix: 60% medium (7B equivalent), 30% large (30B equiv), 10% embeddings / rerank. - Effective tokens/sec per A100 80GB w/ q4x quant: medium=2800 tok/s, large=650 tok/s. - Spot capacity volatility: up to 22% shortfall during procurement windows. - Pre-warm lead: 48-72 hours for snapshotting KV cache and autoscaler warm pools. - Regulatory priority: EU private deployments prioritized for Private offering ramp; dedicated allocation reserved in EU for enterprise customers (10% of regional pool).
demand_scenarios: Scenario A (Conservative): +12% regional growth over 9 months; Scenario B (Expected): +28% growth; Scenario C (Aggressive / Launch): +55% growth concentrated NA->EU after product launch. Each scenario factors 3% monthly uplift baseline + feature-driven spikes tied to product roadmap dates (see linked_artifacts).
trigger_matrix: Soft buffer: 18% utilization headroom remaining -> notify capacity oncall and queue a spot procurement. Hard buffer: 8% headroom remaining -> immediate routing to secondary model tier and turn on burst reserve for 4 hours. KV cold rate >15% -> initiate pre-warm job for top 10 routes. Regional latency P95 > target + 60ms -> push fallback routing to nearest region if within SLO policy. Spot eviction rate > 8% over 6 hours -> suspend spot bidding and promote reserved pools for next 24 hours.
operational_actions: - Week 0: Validate telemetry thresholds against last 6 weeks. - Week 1: Pre-warm top 20 routes in NA and EU for expected ramp. - Week 2-4: Activate 10% burst reserve in APAC if growth exceeds scenario A. - Ongoing: Run heatmap-gen script daily (github link) and publish synthesized runbook to #infra-capacity slack. - Contingency: If hard buffer hit, execute JIRA-OPS-1248 emergency onboarding play (vendor mix switch).
capacity_notes_on_instance_types: - A100 80GB: best for large models; consistent throughput; lower variance. - H100 equivalents: slightly higher peak throughput but higher variability on spot pools; watch thermal throttling on older hardware under sustained 95th percentile load. - T4-like inference instances: use for embeddings and low-latency small models; cheaper but lower per-GPU throughput leads to greater headcount of machines. - Quantization impact: moving medium models to q4x increases effective tok/sec by ~28% but adds 1.4% error rate observed in fidelity tests; operations must map quality budget to cost savings per customer tier.
risks_and_mitigation:
Risk: Large launch concentration in NA saturates KV caches; Mitigation: Canary route split + temporary cache flush cadence + increase cache pre-warm pool.
Risk: Spot supply disruption in EU during vendor maintenance window; Mitigation: Add temporary reserved capacity in EU (10% runway) and cross-region routing policy.
Risk: Underestimated latent feature growth from partner integrations; Mitigation: Create contract clause for committed burst capacity and 24-hr provisioning SLA with platform sales.
